title: Artinian local rings after restriction of a finite residue field extension
statement: Let $k\hookrightarrow l$ be an extension of fields with $[l:k]<\infty$ [def-weil-field]. Let $B$ be a commutative Artinian local ring with specified residue map $\rho:B\twoheadrightarrow l$. Here local means having a unique maximal ideal, and Artinian means satisfying the descending chain condition on ideals. Set $C=B\times_l k=\{(b,t)\in B\times k:\rho(b)=t\text{ in }l\}$ with coordinatewise ring operations. Then $C$ is Artinian local, $C\to k$ is surjective and identifies its residue field with $k$, and the projection $C\to B$ is injective. If $q:B^\prime\twoheadrightarrow B$ is a surjective homomorphism of Artinian local rings with identified residue field $l$, inducing the identity on $l$, then the induced map $B^\prime\times_l k\to B\times_l k$ is surjective and induces the identity on residue field $k$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-ring-self-finite-length], $B$ has finite length as a $B$-module. Apply [lem-exc-semilocal-restriction-length] with its local source ring $A=C$, its semilocal target ring $B$, and its module $M=B$. There is exactly one maximal ideal of $B$, namely $\mathfrak m_B$; its contraction under $j$ is $\mathfrak n$ by the pair description in step 1. The residue map induced by $j$ is exactly $\iota:k\to l$, because $\rho(j(b,t))=\iota(t)$. Its degree is finite by hypothesis. All hypotheses of the cited restriction theorem therefore hold, and its finite-length conclusion gives $\mathrm{length}_C(B)<\infty$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-module-length], choose an integer $N$ bounding the numbers of strict inclusions in chains of $C$-submodules of $B$. An ideal $I$ of $C$ has image $j(I)$ a $C$-submodule of $B$, since $j(c)j(x)=j(cx)$. Injectivity of $j$ makes this assignment preserve and reflect inclusions and strict inclusions. Thus a descending chain of ideals of $C$ can have at most $N$ strict drops; otherwise its first $N+1$ drops, read in reverse order, give too long a strict chain of $C$-submodules of $B$. Every descending chain stabilizes, so $C$ is Artinian.

proof.text: Let $\rho^\prime:B^\prime\twoheadrightarrow l$ be the specified residue map. The condition on $q$ says $\rho q=\rho^\prime$. Consequently $(b^\prime,t)\mapsto(q(b^\prime),t)$ defines a ring homomorphism $C^\prime=B^\prime\times_l k\to C$. Given $(b,t)\in C$, choose $b^\prime$ with $q(b^\prime)=b$. Then $\rho^\prime(b^\prime)=\rho(b)=\iota(t)$, so $(b^\prime,t)\in C^\prime$ maps to $(b,t)$: the map is surjective. Steps 1-3 apply also to $B^\prime$, making $C^\prime$ Artinian local with residue field $k$. The equality $\pi(q(b^\prime),t)=t=\pi^\prime(b^\prime,t)$ shows explicitly that the induced residue-field map is the identity of $k$.
